R269.note: session_regenerate_id() placed after password verification and before the authenticated flags is the correct PHP fixation fix; explanation mis-describes the default as discarding old data (it is copied to the new id) but the code is right.

R270.note: Decodes the gob stream into a DTO without IsAdmin (gob ignores unmatched stream fields) and builds Job with IsAdmin=false, so wire format is preserved and privilege is no longer message-controlled, matching the contract.

R271.note: PasswordEncoder.matches() against the stored hash closes the bypass, but the hardcoded bare $2a$ dummy hash assumes a BCryptPasswordEncoder - under Spring's default DelegatingPasswordEncoder matches() throws IllegalArgumentException on the unknown-username path instead of BadCredentialsException (DaoAuthenticationProvider encodes its dummy via the injected encoder to avoid this).

R272.note: snprintf with sizeof(line) plus a truncation/error check closes the overflow; entries over 63 bytes are now rejected with -1 rather than truncated, which the write-up states plainly and which the original could never log correctly anyway.

R273.note: GetFullPath plus separator-terminated prefix check is the right shape, but the comparison uses OrdinalIgnoreCase on a Linux base path, so on a case-sensitive filesystem a rooted filename like /var/app/Documents/x passes containment while reading a different directory - questionable, not clearly exploitable; the added 404/403 handling is stated.

R274.note: Swaps the branches so non-admins get the user_id-scoped query and admins get Order::all(), exactly the stated contract, with no other change.

R275.note: Handler now checks IsInRole("Admin") via the injected AuthenticationStateProvider before DeleteAccountAsync, so invocation is gated independently of AuthorizeView rendering; non-admins are redirected without deleting, nothing else changes.

R276.note: cookie.setSecure(true) is the whole fix; the unchanged response text still says 'secure flag set to: false', which is now stale but identical to the original output.

R277.note: GetMapping to PostMapping is the correct fix and brings the endpoint under CsrfFilter, but the comment says a settings-page link relies on GET - that link now gets 405 - and the write-up claims functionality is preserved, only obliquely noting the client must now send a token via POST.

R278.note: Parameterized query with the value passed as a Select arg is the right sqlx fix; the ? bindvar assumes MySQL/SQLite (Postgres would need $1 or DB.Rebind), which is a portability nit, not a behaviour change here.

R279.note: RESP multibulk with $len prefixes makes embedded CRLF data rather than a command boundary; verified in the scratch dir with pwsh that Encoding.ASCII emits one byte per UTF-16 char (surrogate pair -> ??) so arg.Length matches the byte count; a null statusMessage now throws NRE where the original sent a malformed inline SET, neither being legitimate use.

R280.note: Prefix check now requires uploadsDir plus filepath.Separator (or exact equality, which the original also permitted), closing the uploads-backup sibling bypass without changing any accepted path.

R281.note: basename() confines the write to the notes directory, which matches the stated no-subdirectory contract; it strips rather than rejects, so ../../etc/passwd is silently saved as notes/passwd - a design nit, not a new weakness, and basename('..') maps to the parent directory where file_put_contents simply fails.

R282.note: AES/GCM/NoPadding with a fresh SecureRandom 12-byte IV prepended to the ciphertext replaces ECB; the output stays a Base64 string decryptable by the key holder and the IV-prefix layout the decryptor needs is stated plainly.

R283.note: Build FAIL: ObjectInputFilter.FilterInfo has serialClass(), not getClassName(), so the change does not compile and the decoder stops working entirely with nothing in the write-up saying so.

R284.note: Switching to Blade {{ }} closes the XSS, but the field is descriptionHtml and the contract asks that allowed rich-text formatting survive if supported - escaping renders any markup as literal text, which the write-up acknowledges as a follow-up (sanitize in the presenter) rather than doing.
